$comment: PreToolUse hook: guard_shell_text.py refuses Bash commands that AUTHOR escape-bearing text
or truncate a file through a shell. The prose rule it enforces was broken ten times in the
project it came from, three of them while the rule was being written down, so it is a hook
and not a paragraph: it fires at the moment of the mistake. Coverage is deliberately narrow
(see the docstring); .claude/hooks/test_guard_shell_text.py pins both halves as a gate
stage. To disable, delete the hooks block -- but read that test first: every BLOCK case is

The command is a POSIX launcher (issue #55): `python` first, `python3` next, and a refusal (exit 2) when neither is on PATH -- Claude Code runs a command hook under sh on Linux/macOS and Git Bash on Windows, and a hook that cannot start would otherwise let every command through. The guard stage runs this string as spelled.

hooks.command: py=python3; command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && py=python; command -v "$py" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "guard_shell_text.py: neither python nor python3 is on PATH; the command is refused" >&2; exit 2; }; exec "$py" "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/guard_shell_text.py"
